subject: Pre-Load progress bar/spinner - as app starts

messages.author: 5b4759b36268c68b
messages.subject: Pre-Load progress bar/spinner - as app starts
parts:
Hi there -

After searching a bit, I'm a little lost.
I've got a shiny app that needs to pull data from a database across the interwebs.
No big deal, as RMySQL works like a charm.  The problem is the traffic delay.  It can take 15-60 seconds to load up.  I only need to load data at startup, doesn't need to be responsive at all.

However, the users can think things are broken & click elsewhere.

I need a progress bar or a spinner to show up - but only as the app starts.  Once the app loads, everything is lickety-split.

I've seen notes and posts about the lovely withProgress() function. I've seen notes about how to implement when the user clicks on a tab, or when the user selects a radio button.

But how do I implement something *before* the user can click on anything?

A lot of the references I found are also a couple of years old.  Concerned about getting a "current" solution.

Any thoughts or directions are helpful.

Thanks!

-Ben

messages.author: 68ce5dd269fd758c
messages.subject: Re: Pre-Load progress bar/spinner - as app starts
parts:
Hi, have you read this post: http://withr.me/add-calculation-in-process-indictor-for-shiny-application/

Not exactly what you need, but you can modify the javascript to run at when loading your shiny-app. 

You may check the status of the webpage using "inspect elements" to make sure what happened when loading data.
